newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs steady in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs steady in slow trade.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices were steady in dull activity late Monday as players stood back to see which direction NYMEX crude oil will take.
NYMEX crude oil futures were up Monday on reports linking Iran to the 1996 bombing of U.S. barracks in Saudi Arabia. NYMEX gasoline was also higher, largely on short covering.
"It's as dead as doornail," said a Houston-based trader. "Sellers are waiting to see if crude will go up further."
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane remained between 34.25 cents and 34.50 cents a gallon, with 34.50 cents sold.
Conway, Kansas, spot material was equally quiet, pegged steady at 34.25/34.50 cents.
Belvieu normal butane also stayed steady at 37.50/38.00 cents. Isobutane was 43.25/43.75 cents.
Conway butane was 34.00/34.50 cents and isobutane 40.75/41.25 cents.
